stem: A test evaluation labels the four groups as A = true positive, B = false positive, C = false negative and D = true negative. Which of the following ratios measures correct negative classification among people without disease?

options.label: A
options.explanation: This ratio is sensitivity, since A and C together represent all actual cases. Specificity instead evaluates correct negative classification among the group without disease.
options.misconception: Uses the diseased-group sensitivity formula to assess disease-free classification.

options.label: B
options.explanation: This ratio is positive predictive value, since A and B together represent all positive results. The requested measure instead begins with people independently known to be disease-free.
options.misconception: Substitutes PPV for specificity by conditioning on positive results.

options.label: C
options.explanation: This ratio is the false-positive fraction among people without disease. It uses the right denominator but counts incorrect positive results rather than correct negative classifications.
options.misconception: Uses the correct noncase denominator but counts false positives as successes.

options.label: D
options.explanation: This ratio is the proportion of actual cases missed by the test. The question asks about correct exclusions among disease-free people, not missed detection among cases.
options.misconception: Counts missed actual cases instead of correctly excluded noncases.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Disease-free people consist of false positives and true negatives, B + D. Correct exclusions are D, so specificity is D divided by B + D.
options.misconception: No misconception: D counts true negatives within the disease-free group B plus D.

context:
Learning objective: Build the specificity denominator from false positives plus true negatives before evaluating screening errors.

Disease-free people consist of false positives and true negatives, B + D. Correct exclusions are D, so specificity is D divided by B + D.
